facts.fact: The page states that self-serve CTV platforms now let political campaigns spending $500 or $5,000 buy contextual inventory, where previously major agency relationships and six-figure minimums were required.
facts.quote: What used to require major agency relationships and six-figure minimums is now available through self-serve platforms for campaigns spending $500 or $5,000.

facts.fact: According to a 2024 IAB study cited by the vendor, 74% of consumers preferred ads placed based on the content they are consuming rather than ads based on tracking their browsing history.
facts.quote: A 2024 IAB study found that 74% of consumers preferred ads placed based on the content they're consuming rather than ads based on tracking their browsing history (IAB, 2024).

facts.fact: The page states that California, Colorado, Connecticut, and Virginia have detailed privacy laws that restrict political campaigns' use of third-party data for targeting voters.
facts.quote: California, Colorado, Connecticut, and Virginia now have detailed privacy laws, and more states are following.

facts.fact: The page says contextual targeting remains allowed almost everywhere on CTV platforms because it does not require individual-level data, even as several platforms introduced stricter political targeting policies in the 2024 cycle.
facts.quote: Several major CTV platforms introduced stricter policies on political ad targeting during the 2024 cycle. Contextual targeting remains allowed almost everywhere

facts.fact: The vendor recommends allocating 20-30% of total campaign budget to the 3-5 calendar moments when a campaign wants to surge, such as debates, conventions, and GOTV weekends.
facts.quote: Allocate 20-30% of total budget to these moments specifically.

facts.fact: The vendor advises planning 3-5 creative rotations per context for political ads.
facts.quote: Plan for 3-5 creative rotations per context.

facts.fact: The vendor states that voters in competitive districts see the same political ads 8-12 times in the final two weeks of a race.
facts.quote: Voters in competitive districts see the same political ads 8-12 times in the final two weeks of a race.

facts.fact: The vendor says contextual political ad buys typically cost 10-25% higher CPM than demographic-only buys.
facts.quote: Typically 10-25% higher CPM.

facts.fact: The vendor says premium contextual placements, such as during debates or high-attention news, can run 50-100% higher than baseline CTV CPMs.
facts.quote: Premium contextual placements, especially during debates or high-attention news moments, can run 50-100% higher than baseline CTV CPMs.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends that campaigns start with their top 3-5 message categories when planning contextual targeting.
facts.quote: Start with your campaign's top 3-5 message categories

facts.fact: The vendor recommends mapping each message to 5-10 content types where that message will land naturally.
facts.quote: write out 5-10 content types where that message will land naturally.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends reviewing CTV placement reports weekly.
facts.quote: Review placement reports weekly to see exactly where your ads ran and adjust as needed.

facts.fact: The vendor says most campaigns find 2-3 context buckets dramatically outperform others, and that shifting budget into them improves cost per vote.
facts.quote: Most campaigns find that 2-3 context buckets dramatically outperform others

facts.fact: The vendor recommends setting brand safety blocklists as exclusions at the account level rather than the campaign level so they carry over between buys.
facts.quote: Lock these in as exclusions at the account level, not the campaign level, so they carry over from buy to buy.

facts.fact: The vendor states that every major CTV platform allows political advertisers to use content-based (contextual) targeting such as genre, publisher, and show-level targeting.
facts.quote: Every major CTV platform allows political advertisers to use content-based targeting (genre, publisher, show-level).

facts.fact: The vendor says some CTV platforms have narrow additional rules for political ads on children's content and on news during breaking tragedies.
facts.quote: Some platforms have additional rules around specific genres (children's content, news during breaking tragedies), but those are narrow exceptions.

facts.fact: The vendor says major CTV platforms are rolling out AI-driven contextual capabilities natively for the 2026 cycle.
facts.quote: Major CTV platforms are rolling out these capabilities natively.

facts.fact: The vendor says most major DSPs support layering voter file matching on top of contextual inventory for political ads.
facts.quote: Most major DSPs support this layered approach.
